summary: Officially retires the printed Assigned Numbers list from RFC 1700, which was a snapshot of protocol parameters from October 1994. Those values are now kept in an online database. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: There used to be a big printed phone book of Internet numbers. It got outdated, so this says to use the always-updated website instead.

questions: where did rfc 1700 assigned numbers go
what replaced the assigned numbers rfc
subtitle: The memo that retired the printed Assigned Numbers RFC in favor of an online database.

tldr.problem: For years the IANA published tables of Internet protocol parameter assignments as "Assigned Numbers" RFCs, but a printed snapshot goes out of date.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3232 notes that the series has been replaced by an online database and officially obsoletes RFC 1700, changing its status to Historic.
tldr.outcome: RFC 1700 is obsolete, and its values are incomplete and in some cases may be wrong. The current values live in the online database instead.

today: RFC 3232 is Informational and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes it. It obsoleted RFC 1700, which it moved to Historic status.

sections.title: The Assigned Numbers Series
sections.content:
From November 1977 through October 1994, the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) periodically published tables of Internet protocol parameter assignments in RFCs titled "Assigned Numbers". The most current of these had Standard status and carried the designation STD 2. At the time of this memo the latest STD 2 is RFC 1700.

That RFC holds an October 1994 snapshot of the assignments.
sections.plainLanguage: For many years the number keepers printed a big list of Internet numbers every so often. The last printed list was from October 1994.

sections.title: RFC 1700 Is Obsoleted
sections.content:
Since 1994, this sequence of RFCs has been replaced by an online database accessible through a web page. The purpose of RFC 3232 is to note this fact and to officially obsolete RFC 1700, whose status changes to Historic.

The memo is blunt about the old list: RFC 1700 is obsolete, and its values are incomplete and in some cases may be wrong. It also says the authors expect the series to be revived in the future by the new IANA organization.
sections.plainLanguage: The printed list is now old news and may have mistakes. Use the live website. The memo adds that the printed list might come back someday.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The memo states that it does not affect the technical security of the Internet. It defines no protocol, so there is nothing further to secure.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo only points to a new place to look things up, so it does not change how safe the Internet is.

references.text: Assigned Numbers, STD 2, RFC 1700, October 1994 (obsoleted by this memo).
